sentiment.rationale: Maersk raised its full-year 2025 underlying EBIT guidance from $0-3bn to $2-3.5bn and EBITDA guidance from $6-9bn to $8-9.5bn, citing more resilient market demand outside North America and a strong first half. The guidance raise is organic, driven by volume growth and operational improvements, not attributed to one-time items or FX. Management expresses confidence in the outlook, noting the Gemini cooperation is on track and terminals are performing strongly, though they acknowledge continued geopolitical uncertainty and a fluid situation in Q4.

summary.revenue: Q2 2025 consolidated revenue of USD 13,130 million, up 2.8% year-on-year (USD 12,771 million in Q2 2024).
summary.eps: Q2 2025 earnings per share of USD 38 (USD 51 in Q2 2024).
summary.guidance: Full-year 2025 underlying EBITDA raised to USD 8.0-9.5bn (previously 6.0-9.0), underlying EBIT raised to USD 2.0-3.5bn (previously 0.0-3.0), free cash flow raised to -1.0 or higher (previously -3.0 or higher). Global container market volume growth revised to 2-4% (previously -1% to 4%). CAPEX unchanged at USD 10-11bn for 2024-2025 and 2025-2026.
summary.margin: Q2 2025 EBITDA margin 17.5% (16.8% in Q2 2024), EBIT margin 6.4% (7.5% in Q2 2024), underlying EBIT margin 6.2% (5.9% in Q2 2024).
key_risks: Unprecedented geopolitical volatility and low visibility into macroeconomic factors.
Continued uncertainty around US trade policy and tariffs (effective container-weighted import tariff estimated at 24% as of 31 July).
Red Sea disruption expected to last for the full year, adding cost from rerouting via Cape of Good Hope.
Supply-demand imbalance in Ocean with excess capacity and pricing pressure; loaded freight rates down 9.6% year-on-year.
North America logistics revenue down 8% year-on-year, impacting Logistics & Services segment.
Elevated macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties impacting container volume growth and freight rates.
key_opportunities: Gemini cooperation successfully phased in, achieving >90% schedule reliability and on track to deliver cost savings in excess of expectations.
Strong volume growth in Ocean (4.2% year-on-year, 10% sequentially) and record-high volumes in Terminals (9.9% year-on-year).
Logistics & Services EBIT margin improving to 4.8% (3.5% in Q2 2024), with continued progress toward 6% target.
Terminals ROIC (LTM) at 15.4%, well above 9% target, with strong performance and investment in expansion.
More resilient market demand outside North America, with China gaining global market share driving container demand.
Strong balance sheet with net cash position of USD 2.5bn and investment-grade ratings.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Management describes 'solid performance,' 'strong execution,' and 'excellent performance' across segments, raises guidance, and expresses confidence in Gemini and cost savings, while acknowledging uncertainty.
